source_note: Degraded-quality variants of an existing real label image, generated by testdata/build_degraded_images.py (Pillow only -- no app/-runtime image-processing libraries required for testdata generation). These fixtures are for FR-039 (image preprocessing: deskew/perspective correction, contrast normalization, glare suppression) and the WBS items that depend on 2.6 -- 6.1 (preprocessing pipeline implementation), 6.8 (Stage 4 unit tests), 16.6 (annotation placement on degraded cases), and 17.4 (edge-case walkthrough). Unlike test_sets.json (WBS 2.3-2.5), this manifest does not define comparison_expectations -- 2.6 traces to image-quality preprocessing, not form-vs-label comparison outcomes. Because each degraded image is a transformation of a label image already used as a label_images entry in test_sets.json, a degraded variant can be substituted for its source image in an existing set (e.g., good_spirits_woodford) for an end-to-end pipeline test: the expectation is that the same comparison_expectations / expected_outcome still hold once preprocessing has run, per FR-039's test ('extraction still succeeds for elements visible in the original').

source_image.note: Selected as the WBS 2.6 source because it is the most heavily reused label image across WBS 2.3-2.5: the primary 'brand' image for good_spirits_woodford (2.3) and reused unchanged in eight WBS 2.4 hard-failure sets (hf_brandname_woodford, hf_fancifulname_woodford, hf_countryoforigin_woodford, hf_14b_woodford, hf_applicantname_woodford, hf_applicantaddress_woodford, hf_netcontents_woodford, hf_abv_woodford). Visible elements: 'KENTUCKY STRAIGHT BOURBON WHISKEY' class/type strip, two barrel icons, 'SELECT BARRELS AGED A SECOND TIME IN CHARRED AMERICAN WHITE OAK BARREL', 'APPROVED BY MASTER DISTILLER' with cursive 'Chris Morris' signature, '45.2% ALC/VOL (90.4 PROOF) 750 mL'.

degraded_images.description: Whole image rotated 8 degrees counter-clockwise with the canvas expanded and corners filled white, simulating a label photographed slightly crooked. All text is fully legible but its baseline is no longer horizontal.
degraded_images.preprocessing_expectation: OpenCV preprocessing should detect the ~8 degree skew (e.g. via minAreaRect on text contours or a Hough-line estimate) and rotate the image back to horizontal before the AI vision call. Because no text is occluded, extraction of every field present on the original image (class/type designation, ABV, proof, net contents, master distiller signature line) should succeed both before and after correction -- this fixture isolates the deskew step from the contrast/glare steps below.

degraded_images.description: A soft, blurred-edge white ellipse (peak opacity ~69%, not fully opaque) is composited over the upper-right quadrant, simulating a camera-flash reflection off the label. Text under the glare ('...GHT BOURBON WHISKEY', 'APPROVED BY MASTER DISTILLER', the 'Chris Morris' signature) is faded to a low-contrast 'ghost' but the underlying pixel data is not destroyed; text outside the glare zone (barrel icons, 'SELECT BARRELS...' paragraph, ABV/proof/net-contents) remains fully legible.
degraded_images.preprocessing_expectation: OpenCV preprocessing should identify the over-bright region (e.g. thresholding on a luminance channel) and apply local contrast normalization (CLAHE) to recover the faded text within it. Per FR-039's test, extraction must still succeed for elements visible in the original outside the glare zone regardless of whether the glare-affected text is fully recovered; this fixture isolates the glare-suppression step from the deskew/contrast steps above and below.

degraded_images.description: Brightness reduced to 35% and contrast reduced to 75% of the original, simulating a dimly-lit/underexposed photo. All text remains in its original position and is technically present in the pixel data, but at very low contrast against the also-darkened background.
degraded_images.preprocessing_expectation: OpenCV preprocessing should apply contrast normalization / histogram equalization (e.g. CLAHE) to restore the brightness and contrast range needed for the AI vision call to read all text. Because no region is rotated or occluded, this fixture isolates the contrast-normalization step from the deskew/glare steps above.

degraded_images.description: The glare overlay (as in woodford_front_glare.jpg, sized against the original frame) is applied first, then the result is rotated 8 degrees with expand=True and white fill -- combining a crooked photo with a flash reflection. This matches FR-039's literal test phrasing, 'a label image photographed at an angle with glare.'

parameters.overlay_shape: ellipse, center at (0.7w, 0.3h), radii (0.28w, 0.4h), computed before rotation

degraded_images.preprocessing_target: Full FR-039 pipeline (deskew/perspective correction + contrast normalization + glare suppression)
degraded_images.preprocessing_expectation: This is the FR-039 acceptance-test fixture: OpenCV preprocessing should deskew the image AND suppress/normalize the glare region in either order, and the AI vision call should still successfully extract the elements visible in the original outside the glare zone (barrel icons, 'SELECT BARRELS...' paragraph, ABV/proof/net-contents), per FR-039's test wording verbatim.
